title: Differences between related forms emerge gradually and are small in the young

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Differences between related forms emerge gradually and are small in the young

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because form differences are attained by growth at specific velocities over long periods, differences between any two related individuals or species must appear gradually and be little apparent in the young, and animals of very different adult size differ less and less in size and form when traced back through foetal stages.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. III: The Rate of Growth

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it is accordingly obvious that in any two related individuals (whether specifically identical or not) the differences between them must manifest themselves gradually, and be but little apparent in the young. It is for the same simple reason that animals which are of very different sizes when adult, differ less and less in size (as well as in form) as we trace them backwards through the foetal stages.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter III, “The Rate of Growth”; topic “Darwin and embryonic resemblance”. Scope: related individuals and species, especially mammals with foetal development

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch03-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Developmental disparity is directly measurable, and open image repositories provide useful series for selected vertebrate clades. Coverage is insufficient for the universal any-two-related-forms wording and comparative staging introduces substantial judgment.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure pairwise morphological and size disparity between related taxa at matched embryonic, fetal and adult stages, and test whether disparity generally increases with developmental time. Large early-stage differences or decreasing disparity toward adulthood would refute the prediction for those pairs.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Comparable stages and structures across species are difficult to align.

Embryos of related species are unevenly sampled.

Development can include early divergence followed by convergence.

fields.value:

data existence: 0.65

discriminating power: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Age-related disparity is a standard morphometric question, and some public ontogenetic series bear on it. The claim covers related individuals and species, especially mammals traced through fetal stages, and fetal series of that breadth are not in one open collection. Existing scans can test a biased subset, with a real risk that preservation, not biology, produces the gradual pattern.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure size and shape disparity among related species at successive ages, including fetal stages. Disparity small in the young and increasing toward the adult would support the claim; disparity already large at the earliest comparable stages would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Museum sampling favors adults, which can exaggerate apparent late divergence.

Fetal and juvenile series are taxonomically sparse next to adult specimens.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.45

operationalizability: 0.8
